one_line: A 7 second clip of a newborn on a crib sheet curling onto their side, with text saying it is the 'newborn curl' and not a sign of rolling, and the full explanation left to the caption.

hook.visual: Close, slightly overhead shot of a newborn in a beige ribbed bodysuit lying on a cream sheet with a pacifier near the top edge, giving a serious sideways frown.
hook.on_screen_text: Have you ever noticed your newborn curling up like this when you lay them down?
hook.why_it_stops_the_scroll: A direct question describes a behaviour new parents have seen, while the newborn's frown is already in frame and the 'like this' is about to be shown. The text is centred and legible muted.

beats.observed: Newborn on the back, head turned to the side, serious look, hands near the chest, legs bent. Centred white text across the body.
beats.on_screen_text: Have you ever noticed your newborn curling up like this when you lay them down?

beats.observed: The newborn turns toward a side-lying curl, hands up near the face and knees drawn up. A hand-drawn coral arrow pointing down appears at the right. The question text is replaced.
beats.on_screen_text: It's not a sign of rolling.

beats.observed: The curl continues: hands beside the face and ear, legs bent and swinging to the side, the body tilted but not rolled over. The arrow and text stay.
beats.on_screen_text: It's not a sign of rolling.

beats.observed: Newborn lies mostly on the back with both arms raised beside the head and a slight smile; legs bent. Two-line centred text with a down-arrow emoji pointing to the caption.
beats.on_screen_text: That's called the newborn curl. Here's why it happens ⬇️

payoff: The name of the behaviour ('the newborn curl') lands at about 6.0 s. The actual explanation (flexed muscles carried over from the fetal position, a reflex that fades) is only in the caption, not in the video.
cta: 'Here's why it happens' with a down-arrow emoji at 6.0 to 7.4 s, pointing viewers to the caption. No follow, link or comment ask.
share_or_comment_trigger: Shares are the signal: 1,858 shares is about 49 percent of the 3,782 likes and 0.39 percent of 472,600 views, which fits parents sending this to a partner or friend with a newborn who asked whether the baby is rolling (inferred). Comments are only 26.
why_it_worked: Large outlier: 472,600 views is 147.8x the account median of 3,196.5, with the strongest like rate of these four videos (0.8 percent) and shares at roughly half of likes.
One narrow, misread behaviour (curl mistaken for rolling) is corrected in 7 s, so a very short clip likely replays and finishes (inferred, no retention data in the file).
The hook question describes exactly what is on screen, and the deferred explanation plus search-style phrases in the caption push viewers to read, share or search.
paid_signal: no: like rate 0.8 percent is above the 0.3 percent flag and shares are very high relative to likes, consistent with organic spread; spend cannot be ruled out from the data.

solo_route.how: 1) Ask a parent who is a customer, ambassador or friend for a 5 to 10 s clip of their child doing one recognisable developmental behaviour (written permission first), or collect it through the UGC creator form. 2) Have a barter pediatric nurse or developmental specialist confirm the one-line explanation in writing. 3) In CapCut, lay centred light text: a question describing the behaviour (0 to 3 s), a hand-drawn arrow sticker plus a correction line (3 to 6 s), then a name for the behaviour and a down-arrow pointer to the caption (6 s to end). 4) Put the explanation and Hebrew search phrases in the caption, with a one-line mention of LumeBook at the very end.
solo_route.needs: Real child footage with written parental consent (or a UGC clip with usage rights) and a barter expert or cited source to verify the developmental claim. The explanation is not verified here; the account's caption claims are unconfirmed.

The expert-checked explanation lives in the caption, with a soft LumeBook mention at the end.

evidence_notes: Whisper output is only '(upbeat music)' from 0 to 2.58 s, so there is no usable speech transcript; no speech is claimed and sound is not described. All beats are observed from 8 frames at 1 s steps; the on-screen text and coral arrow were read directly and are fully legible. The medical claim (muscles flexed from the fetal position, reflex fades, not rolling) comes only from the caption and was not verified. made_by is unclear because the footage source is not stated. loop_ending is inferred from the 7.4 s length. The baby is not identified.
